newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Two Austrian insurers pave way for merger.
newsitem.headline: Two Austrian insurers pave way for merger.

text.p: Two leading Austrian insurers, Bundeslaender and Austria-Collegialitaet said on Monday they would strive to strengthen their business abroad through a planned holding and do not rule out merging altogether.

"We must endeavour to move into other markets.... and for that one needs a certain operating weight," said Herbert Schimetschek, designated chairman of the planned holding company BARC Versicherungs-Holding AG, which will hold at least 50.1 percent of both Austria and Bundeslaender.

"It is possible that the holding company is an interim model for several years which ends with a merger," said Walter Rothensteiner, chairman of Raiffeisen Zentralbank Oesterreich and future member of the board at BARC.
Schimetschek said efforts would focus on strengthening business in the Czech and Slovak Republics, Slovenia, southern Germany and northern Italy.
Bundeslaender, which is majority owned by the Raiffeisen group, last year reported a premium income of 20 billion schillings.
Austria-Collegialitaet is the country's leading health insurer and had a premium income of seven billion schillings last year. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12 253
